chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad narrated to me from his father from Muhammad ibn Ahmad who said: Yusuf ibn Ismail narrated to me through his chain to him who said:

Indeed, when a believer has a fever, if it is a single fever, his sins scatter from him like the leaves of a tree. If he is on his bed, his groaning is Tasbih and his cries are Tahleel, and his turning on his bed is like one who strikes with his sword in the way of Allah. If he faces [Allah] worshipping among his brothers and companions, he will be forgiven. So good news for him if he repents, and woe to him if he returns [to sin]. And well-being is more beloved to us.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for a believer who suffers from a fever according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the concept of *sabr* (patience) during illness, where the physical manifestations of fever—such as groaning and restlessness—are elevated to the status of continuous dhikr and jihad. This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on the transformative power of suffering, linking bodily pain directly to spiritual purification and the expiation of sins, while noting that despite these rewards, divine health remains preferable. The text serves as a comfort to the sick, framing their bedridden state as an active engagement in worship rather than passive suffering.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 3. It was narrated to me by al-Hussain b. Ahmad from his father from Muhammad b. Ahmad who said it was narrated to me by Yusif b. Ismail through his chain to him who said:

“If a believer has fever once, his sins are destroyed like dry leaves fall off in the wind. His cries on his bed are like Tasbih and moans like praising Allah. His turning left and right is like fighting with sword in the way of Allah. If he worships Allah along with his brothers and friends, he will be forgiven. If he repents, he is indeed fortunate and if he breaks repentance, he is ill-fated. Any way, we prefer his well being and salvation.”
